existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `SubstanceSpecification` has material local breaking changes from R4 to the R6 ballot: the same-named resource is gone and the probable successor is `SubstanceDefinition`. The biggest migration concerns are the root resource rename, remodeled property/relationship/source-material content, and loss or restructuring of specialized companion-resource references. Confidence is high for structural deltas from local packages, but official mapping and terminology expansions would improve migration guidance.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is not a simple resourceType rename. Implementers need a version-aware transform that first maps `SubstanceSpecification` to `SubstanceDefinition`, then rewrites local children with changed names and content models. The highest-risk areas are substance properties, relationships, specialized companion references, source/representation documents, molecular weight/isotope data, and status/name-language conformance semantics. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy unless extensions or companion-resource mappings are defined for R6-only content.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the same-named R6 artifact is absent and that `SubstanceDefinition` is the successor candidate because this is directly supported by package indexes, the R6 StructureDefinition, and the R6 `fhir-old-types` code system. Confidence is lower for some semantic mappings because no official diff, StructureMap, ConceptMap, narrative migration guide, or terminology expansions were available.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
SubstanceSpecification has a resource-identity break: SubstanceSpecification is not present as an R6 resource; the probable successor is SubstanceDefinition. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 97/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.

topFindings.title: Specialized R4 substance companion references were removed or folded into the new model
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid with R6-to-R4 loss: old reference elements become unknown in R6, old target resource types are absent, and R6 inline source-material data cannot be represented as the old R4 reference without creating another resource or preserving data elsewhere.

topFindings.title: Property backbone was remodeled: optional code became mandatory type, string values and defining substance details were removed
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 properties missing `code`, using `amountString`, or carrying removed child elements are not valid R6 `SubstanceDefinition.property` content after a mechanical rename.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Relationship backbone now requires a relationship type and narrows amount/reference details
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 relationship repetitions without a relationship code or with `amountRange` fail the R6 content model unless curated or transformed.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
